jess_support: FYI — GizmoCorp (dedicated pool dp-7) reports repeated latency spikes around 00:00 UTC and a mix of 429s + occasional 503s. Ticket SUP-10234. Any quick triage steps? :eyes:
ryan_eng: Can you paste a sample request/headers and the exact error payload? also want the x-rw-* headers from the response if available.
jess_support: Payload is a nightly batch POST to /v1/generate, about ~700 concurrent short requests (avg 120 tokens). Sample curl we captured:
```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-rl-large","input":"...","max_tokens":128}'
```
Responses we saw: 429 with headers `x-rw-remaining: 0`, `x-rw-limit: 500`, `x-rw-reset: 1672531205`, and sometimes 503 with body "capacity temporarily unavailable".
maria_sre: That header pattern screams reserved-pool token exhaustion. dp-7 is configured with reserved_tokens=500 and a refill window every minute, but a cron job at 00:00 unrolls a bunch of jobs so short bursts exceed bucket and queueing drops to 429s. Check dedicated metrics: gpool_util and reserved_pool_tokens.
sam_prod: Customer also reported a billing/auth glitch — some of their fallback calls to a hosted fallback model returned 401. Their API key is scoped to the dedicated pool only; when our router fell back to hosted variant it rejected the key. So two-fold: throughput caps + fallback/auth mismatch.
ryan_eng: Repro plan: 1) run a localized load loop from our staging runner to dp-7 using same token pattern (script below) 2) capture /metrics (gpool_util, qps, inflight) and nginx/access headers 3) capture request/response headers for first 60s
Local load loop (k6 or simple bash):
```
for i in {1..700}; do 
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test-REDACTED" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-rl-large","input":"x","max_tokens":16}' &
done
wait
```
maria_sre: Short-term mitigations we can apply now: 1) increase headroom for dp-7 by bumping reserved_tokens to 750 (console API patch) 2) enable per-customer smoothing rule so bursts are spread across 60s window (policy: burst_smoothing=true, window=60s) 3) patch router to avoid switching to hosted fallback when key is scoped to dedicated pools (fail-safe to return 429/notify instead of 401).
ryan_eng: Config patch example (console api):
```
PATCH /v1/dedicated/pools/dp-7
{ "reserved_tokens": 750, "burst_policy": { "mode":"smooth", "window_s":60 } }
```
sam_prod: For the billing/auth side we should note: customer was charged for fallback calls (their billing caused confusion). We need to add a safeguard: if key scope != destination scope then do not route to alternative billing tier. Create SUP-10235 to handle billing protection/route rules.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: deploy completed for routing-v2 at 2364829200 by ryan_eng :white_check_mark:
maria_sre: Longer-term: add a midnight job to top-off reserved pools after cron windows and add telemetry alert when x-rw-remaining < 50 for >30s. Also add a dashboard panel showing per-pool refill rate and synthetic batch test at 00:05.
jess_support: I'll notify the customer of temporary mitigation (bumped tokens + smoothing) and request they shift their batch to a staggered schedule as well. I'll attach the load logs and our repro instructions to SUP-10234.
ryan_eng: I'll follow up with a post-deploy run and attach traces (span ids) to the ticket. If we still see 503 after the bump, we'll open an infra incident.
sam_prod: Created internal ticket SUP-10235 for billing/auth guard rails.
jess_support: Thanks all — keeping this thread open while we validate. :thumbsup:
